sections.title: Culture of Honor and Personal-Professional Congruence

summary: Jeanne Bliss argues that beloved companies win by choosing trust over control: they treat customers as trustworthy and replace excessive rules with innovation and partnership, while empowering employees to do the right thing rather than micromanaging every action. The talk contrasts policy-heavy, price-driven competition with a culture that emphasizes Energy, collaboration, and long-term loyalty. Bliss also suggests that employees stay and thrive when the organization honors them and when corporate decisions align with personal values, citing Land’s End as an example of congruence between business choices and lived life. The result is a customer- and employee-centric culture built on trust, autonomy, and shared purpose.
title: Trust-Driven Culture: Customers and Employees at the Core
